title: Smooth proper models of one-variable fields over an algebraically closed field
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field (every nonconstant polynomial over $k$ has a root) [def-weil-field], and let $E/k$ be a finitely generated field extension of transcendence degree one [def-kun-transcendence-degree]. There exists a smooth integral proper finite-type $k$-scheme $C$ of dimension one [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] and a $k$-isomorphism $k(C)\cong E$, where $k(C)$ is the local ring at the generic point. For every valuation ring $B\subseteq E$ [def-trf-valuation-ring] containing $k$ and having fraction field $E$ (equivalently, for each $x\in E^\times$, either $x\in B$ or $x^{-1}\in B$), the generic-point morphism $\operatorname{Spec}E\to C$ extends to a $k$-morphism $\operatorname{Spec}B\to C$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum].

source.place: Tag 0BY1 (theorem-curves-rational-maps), existence of a normal projective model, and Tag 0BY3 (lemma-nonsingular-model-smooth), smoothness over a perfect field; the final clause is the proper valuative criterion (lemma-nagata-proper-valuative-criterion-existence-api).

proof.text: Choose field generators $e_1,\ldots,e_r$ of $E/k$. Apply [lem-trf-field-generators-affine-model] to obtain $U=\operatorname{Spec}k[e_1,\ldots,e_r]$, its closed immersion into $\mathbb A^r_k$, and the $k$-isomorphism $\theta:k(U)\cong E$. This $U$ is integral and finite type, and $\dim U=\operatorname{trdeg}_kE=1$ by the hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0BXN, essential-surjectivity paragraph, with 00P0; old steps 1--2

proof.text: The field $k$ is perfect. To see this in the sense needed by the normalization theorem, let $\alpha$ be algebraic over $k$ in any extension. Its irreducible minimal polynomial has a root $a\in k$ by algebraic closedness. Division by $T-a$ and irreducibility force that polynomial to have degree one. Hence $\alpha\in k$ and is separable over $k$. Every algebraic extension of $k$ is therefore separable.

Apply [lem-trf-normalized-projective-closure] to this $U$, its specified affine-space closed immersion, and the perfect field $k$ from step 2. For the projective closure $X$ and its normalization $C$, this gives an integral smooth proper finite-type $k$-scheme $C$ of dimension one and a $k$-isomorphism $\psi:k(C)\cong k(U)$. Choose $\theta\circ\psi:k(C)\cong E$. The same $C$ and same field isomorphism will be used for every valuation ring.

source.place: Tags 0BY1, final compactify-then-normalize alternative, and 0BY3; old steps 3--4 and 6

proof.text: Fix a valuation ring $B\subseteq E$ as in the corrected statement, with $k\subseteq B$ and $\operatorname{Frac}B=E$. Compose the isomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}E\cong\operatorname{Spec}k(C)$ with the generic-point morphism to $C$. This is a $k$-morphism, since the function-field isomorphism is over $k$. The maps induced by $k\subseteq B\subseteq E$ give a commutative square with upper arrow $\operatorname{Spec}E\to C$, lower arrow $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, and right arrow the proper structural morphism of $C$. Apply [lemma-nagata-proper-valuative-criterion-existence-api] with $(Y,S,A,K)=(C,\operatorname{Spec}k,B,E)$. Its extension is precisely a $k$-morphism $\operatorname{Spec}B\to C$ restricting to the prescribed generic-point morphism. This works for every such $B$, including $B=E$.
